subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
passage:
Vasudha: The whole floor is whispering about the wrong report I sent
Sonali: Are you okay?
Vasudha: Face burning. I almost skipped the stand-up 😔
Sonali: But you went?
Vasudha: I went. I said "I sent the wrong figures yesterday. Corrected ones went out this morning, and I'll get a second check before the next ones." Nobody said a word
Sonali: How was it?
Vasudha: Ten seconds of awful. Then it was just work. Someone even said they made the same mistake in their first year 🙂
Sonali: And the whispering?
Vasudha: I'll let it be. I can't fix what they say. I can fix the report
Sonali: Dinner tonight?
Vasudha: Yes please. I'm buying

qa.q: What did Vasudha say in the stand-up about the report?
qa.a: Vasudha said the wrong figures went out yesterday and corrected ones went out this morning.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling before the stand-up?
qa.a: Vasudha felt embarrassed and ashamed, with a burning face, enough to almost skip the meeting.

qa.q: What did Vasudha do that turned the shame into something manageable?
qa.a: Vasudha stated the facts plainly, sent the corrected figures and arranged a second check, then let the whispering pass instead of chasing it.

qa.q: How might a colleague have felt when they heard Vasudha state the mistake?
qa.a: A colleague who shared having made the same mistake in their first year likely felt understanding and relief that it was handled as ordinary work.

grounding: A young adult gossiped about lets shame pass, states the facts plainly and repairs what can be repaired.

subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
passage: At the tea stall, Uday heard his name and the word "careless", and his ears burned. For three days he had written the wrong milk weights in the dairy cooperative's register. That evening at the village meeting he stood up. "I wrote wrong weights for three days. The mistake is mine. I have the register. Tomorrow I will come to each house and correct every entry in front of you." Madhuri, who supplied milk from six buffaloes, said, "Bring your pen at six." A few people still talked. Uday went from house to house, and by Sunday the register matched what each family remembered. He stopped counting who whispered and went back to weighing the milk.

qa.q: How many days had Uday written the wrong milk weights?
qa.a: Uday had written the wrong milk weights for three days.

qa.q: What was Uday feeling when he heard the word 'careless' at the tea stall?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and exposed, shown by his burning ears.

qa.q: What did Uday do at the meeting and afterwards to deal with the shame?
qa.a: He stated the mistake plainly, owned it and went from house to house correcting every entry, so his conduct answered the gossip.

qa.q: What might Madhuri's reply say about how the villagers saw Uday's offer?
qa.a: Telling Uday to bring the pen at six suggests Madhuri accepted the offer and treated the correction as something worth doing properly.

grounding: A young adult gossiped about tells the facts plainly and repairs what can be repaired without waiting for others' opinions.
